instruction: Check the word count of the essay document "Recruitment_and_retention_of_health_professionals_across_Europe.docx" in /home/user and verify that it contains at least 8000 words as required for the submission. If it does, add a text note at the end of the document stating "Word count requirement met: [actual count] words" and save the file.

metadata.explanation: Task requires checking word count and conditionally adding a note. The evaluator enforces the conditional logic: 'If word count >= 8000, THEN add note and save file'. Verification: Actual document contains 8702 words (verified by Python script), which exceeds the 8000 word minimum requirement.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Conditional scoring enforced: 0.0 if word_count < 8000 (requirement not met); 1.0 if word_count >= 8000 AND note 'Word count requirement met: [number] words' exists at end (full completion); 0.3 if word_count >= 8000 BUT no note (partial - requirement identified but conditional action not completed).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks ALL requirements: (1) word count >= 8000, and (2) conditional note addition
Getter logic is correct: extracts both word_count and last_paragraph from DOCX file using python-docx library
Metric logic is correct: properly enforces conditional instruction semantics (docx__f3c1df34.py:52-62)
Conditional scoring properly implemented: 0.0 if word_count < 8000, 1.0 if word_count >= 8000 AND note exists, 0.3 if word_count >= 8000 but no note added
Regex pattern correctly verifies note format: 'word count requirement met: [digits] words' (case-insensitive, flexible spacing)
File save requirement implicitly verified: if note appears in last_paragraph after postconfig sleep, file was saved
Expected value 'min_words: 8000' is semantically correct for the 8000 word requirement
Edge cases handled: empty file returns word_count=0, exceptions caught and return default values
Minor: Regex doesn't verify the number in note matches actual word count, but this is acceptable for practical verification
